title: The Baby Medicine That Was Really Morphine

sections.name: The Baby Medicine That Was Really Morphine
lines: In the 1800s, exhausted parents had a secret weapon for a crying baby. Mrs Winslow's Soothing Syrup.
It was sold for teething babies, and the adverts promised a peaceful night for the whole family.
It made babies sleepy, all right. But a little too much could stop a baby from waking up at all.
In 1911, the American Medical Association called it a baby killer.
Laws changed, labels improved, and the morphine was eventually taken out.
